description: How to read AutoSA latency. The paper number is the max of module latencies plus the last drain tile. Kernel min, kernel max, and loop II are different columns.

skills.pattern: the model estimate is compared to kernel Worst-caseLatency or to a single loop II
skills.strategy: Section 7.2 defines design latency as the maximum of the module latencies. predict_design_latency takes that maximum and adds the last drain tile. Report that number as the paper latency. Keep HLS kernel min and HLS kernel max in their own columns. Module-max versus the model is still unmeasured on the U280 300 MHz run: HLS jobs 3464450, 3464453, and 3464456 wrote 0 candidates.
required_steps: take the max of the per-module latencies from latency_est
store kernel min and kernel max separately from that paper latency
guards: do not raise this skill to high until a completed HLS run reports max of module LatencyBest
the 5% paper band is not the same claim as within 10% of kernel min

skills.pattern: ranking or the paper error uses csynth kernel max
skills.strategy: Kernel worst-case latency is the dataflow summary. On the ge64 set the kernel-max over model is often about 2x, and only a minority of rows are within 10%. That is a different metric from section 7.2.
required_steps: do not rank the paper model on kernel max
if kernel max is shown, label it HLS kernel max
guards: a close kernel min does not make the kernel max the paper latency

skills.pattern: a loop II of 1, or a module interval in the thousands, is reported as the design latency
skills.strategy: Loop II is the initiation interval of a pipelined loop. On these MM designs it is mostly 1 and sometimes 2 or 3. The thousands-scale number is a latency, not an II. The generic HLS pack may still target II=1; this skill only forbids using II as the AutoSA latency.
required_steps: record loop II only in an II column
record kernel min, kernel max, and module max as latencies
guards: do not quote a module interval as II

skills.pattern: a double-buffered I/O module is estimated as inter plus intra for every design
skills.strategy: If the module is double-buffered, latency is outer * max(inter, intra) plus intra when in==1, otherwise plus inter. Otherwise it is outer * (inter + intra). At N>=512 the HLS max follows outer*max plus one side, not the sum.
required_steps: use the double-buffer formula when module_prop double_buffer is 1
do not replace that formula with inter+intra for large N
guards: B_IO_L2_in and C_IO_L2_out are the modules where this showed up

skills.pattern: an outer latency of 0 on a double-buffered module is replaced by a nonzero constant for every design
skills.strategy: predict_module_latency_xilinx sets latency to 0 when an outer module hits a user node while latency is still 1, which drops one child. Change that only when the outer skeleton has no loops. The empty-outer case is the mm64 ST4 I/O gap. It is not the N>=512 pattern.
required_steps: treat outer 0 as a bug only when the outer loop skeleton is empty
do not add a nonzero outer trip to designs whose outer loop is already nonzero
guards: do not change the double-buffer formula in the same edit

skills.pattern: a non-numeric loop lower bound such as p0 is replaced by a nonzero constant to close a latency gap
skills.strategy: The latency reader sets a non-numeric lower bound to 0 and rejects a non-numeric upper bound. Trip count is ub-lb+1 after that. If the JSON upper bound disagrees with the HLS trip, the fix belongs in the compiler that writes latency_est, not in a different substituted constant.
required_steps: compare the JSON ub with the HLS trip before editing the estimator
guards: substituting a nonzero lower bound makes the estimate smaller and does not repair a short JSON upper bound

skills.pattern: DRAM latency is left at 200 ns, or the search cycle_period differs from the HLS clock
skills.strategy: The paper uses 182 ns of DRAM latency. The estimator divides 182 by cycle_period. Designs 4 and 5 are 300 MHz, which is 3.33 ns in this flow. The search cycle_period and AUTOSA_CLOCK_NS must be that same number. The earlier mm1024 optimizer file used cycle_period 5.
required_steps: set search cycle_period equal to the HLS clock period
guards: changing 5 ns to 3.33 ns changes DRAM cycles; it does not by itself rewrite a compute-bound module latency

skills.pattern: space-time 4 is described as either within the paper's 5% or as a uniform miss
skills.strategy: On mm1024, 8 of 10 space-time 4 rows are within 10% of the model on HLS kernel min. That band is kernel min, not the paper module-max. Do not copy this sentence onto space-time 5.
required_steps: quote the space-time 4 kernel-min band only for kernel min
leave the paper 5% claim unmet until module LatencyBest is collected
guards: space-time 5 at mm1024 is about 3x to 4x on kernel min, with no within-10% row in the ge64 set

skills.pattern: space-time 5 is reported inside the paper's 5% latency band
skills.strategy: Space-time 5 is the (j,k) array. The paper does not report it. On the measured kernel min, mm1024 space-time 5 is about 3x to 4x the model, and the long module is C_IO_L2_out. The ge64 space-time 5 set has no within-10% row.
required_steps: report space-time 5 kernel min as a miss band
name C_IO_L2_out when that module is the long one
guards: do not merge space-time 4 and space-time 5 into one accuracy sentence
